items.abstract: <jats:p><p>Fake News has been spreading widely throughout the world as the booming internet era has started worldwide. Now, more people have access to the Internet than ever, which has led to a significant rise in spreading fake news. So, to solve this issue, it would be highly impossible to manually remove every phony news article. To tackle the above problem of checking on information related to the source, content, or news publisher to categorize it as genuine or fake, we take the help of Machine Learning to classify the information on the web as True or False. Therefore this paper explores the different types of ML classifiers to detect fake news. Therefore, this study will use textual properties of the news dataset we took from Kaggle to distinguish a piece of news as fake or real. Furthermore, with these properties, we will train our model using different ML classification algorithms to evaluate the performance of the dataset collected.</p></jats:p>
title: A Comparative Study of Hybrid Machine Learning Approaches for Fake News Detection that Combine Multi-Stage Ensemble Learning and NLP-based Framework

items.abstract: <jats:p>The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and cyber-physical systems has led to an exponential increase in multi-modal sensor data, necessitating robust and intelligent anomaly detection frameworks to ensure system integrity, safety, and security. Traditional anomaly detection methods often fall short due to their inability to effectively fuse heterogeneous data streams, capture complex spatiotemporal dependencies, or adapt to the dynamic nature of real-time data. This research presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates the strengths of K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to address these critical challenges. Our proposed system leverages a multi-stage architecture: first, a data fusion layer harmonizes disparate sensor modalities (e.g., vibration, temperature, acoustic, and visual signals) using a feature extraction and alignment mechanism. Subsequently, a sliding window technique feeds this fused data into a hybrid KNN-LSTM model, where KNN operates as an efficient, non-parametric filter to identify local proximity-based outliers, while the LSTM component models long-term temporal sequences to detect subtle, context-dependent deviations that manifest over time. Crucially, we integrate streaming analytics capabilities, employing an online learning strategy that allows the model to incrementally update its decision boundaries without full retraining, thereby maintaining high detection accuracy in non-stationary environments. The efficacy of this framework is evaluated on a benchmark industrial sensor dataset, demonstrating a significant improvement in precision and recall over standalone models, particularly in reducing false positives in noisy, high-velocity data streams. The findings underscore the potential of hybrid KNN-LSTM architectures as a scalable and accurate solution for real-time anomaly detection across diverse critical infrastructure and smart manufacturing applications.</jats:p>
title: AI Use in Anomaly Detection: Integrating Multi-Modal Sensor Data and Streaming Analytics Using Hybrid KNN-LSTM Networks
